newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 14.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Thursday:
IRISH INDEPENDENT

- Former prime minister Albert Reynolds will run for the presidency even if SDLP leader John Hume enters the race - Fruit of the Loom chief Willie McCarter has been served with a redundancy notice as has his brother John and finance director Seamus McEleney.
- Irish pound gains as EMU rumours hit sterling
- IMO plans listings and two million punt zinc spend
- Norwich gets Dublin listing today

- Jobs fear as local traders object to 20 million punt tourist plan - Ryanair is confident its British rival Easyjet will not secure control of Luton Airport to which the Irish airline flies up to four times daily - Shareholders back capital revamp at a First Ireland extraordinary meeting
IRISH TIMES
- Further early releases of IRA prisoners considered
- Church to stress parents' role in sexuality courses
- Fruit of the Loom men to fight for their jobs
- UK rates may rise further warns the Bank of England
- Financials takes a battering as the continental markets slump
- DuPont to expand in Derry
- Irish pound gains ground as sterling meets with some heavy selling
- Jobless in Northern Ireland at 17-year low point
THE EXAMINER
- Government moves to cement truce by release of two IRA men
- Maze riot leaves 19 in sick bay
- Listing means tax breaks for Norwich Union shareholders
